transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-22
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE), Markus Chen (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Summit - Head Security), Rajiv Menon (CTO), Tom Reed (Procurement)

Summary (auto-generated):
Discovery focused on security posture and deployment options: SOC2, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs/retention, KMS/HSM encryption, and private/VPC deployment constraints. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private; main blockers: strict data residency + audit evidence and KMS control. Next steps agreed: send SOC2 pack and architecture diagram, schedule POC for private deployment.

Topics:
- SOC2 / ISO compliance and evidence
- Authentication: SSO / SAML / SCIM
- Authorization: RBAC, tenant isolation
- Audit logs, retention, SIEM integration
- Encryption and KMS/HSM control
- Deployment: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC / on-prem)
- Data retention & deletion policies

Transcript:
[00:00] Aisha (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros? I'm Aisha, I'm the AE on this account, and Markus is our solutions engineer.
[00:07] Markus (Redwood SE): Hey all, Markus here, I work on security and infra for Redwood's private and dedicated offerings.
[00:12] Lena (Summit): Hi, Lena Ortiz, head of security at Summit Finance.
[00:15] Rajiv (Summit): Rajiv Menon, CTO.
[00:17] Tom (Summit): Tom Reed from procurement.
[00:20] Aisha: Great. The purpose today is a security posture discovery - want to understand your must-haves for SOC2, SSO, KMS, data residency, that sort of thing. Lina - sorry, Lena - do you want to kick off with your high-level requirements?
[00:34] Lena: Sure. We are in the middle of a vendor review for any system that will process PII or financial data. Primary blockers are: we need SOC 2 Type II evidence, long-term audit logs shipped to our SIEM, SSO with SAML and SCIM provisioning (Okta), KMS control or ability to bring your own key, and data residency in our EU region. Also need fine-grained RBAC and separation between test and prod.
[00:56] Aisha: Good, that's clear. Markus, can you talk about Redwood's current posture?
[01:02] Markus: Yep. At a high level: our hosted API is SOC 2 Type II - we can share the report under NDA - and we support SSO via SAML/Okta plus SCIM for provisioning. For encryption, we support envelope encryption at rest and you can integrate your KMS - we support AWS KMS and HSM-backed keys for private deployments. For audit logs, we provide detailed request logs, token usage, and admin activity logs; logs can be exported to S3 and integrated with customers' SIEM (we have connectors for Splunk/Datadog).
[01:35] Rajiv: When you say "integrate your KMS", do we get control of the master key, or is it more of a wrapped key model? We need to be able to revoke keys on our side quickly.
[01:44] Markus: For Redwood Hosted we support a BYOK pattern using AWS KMS in the customer's account - you can hold the CMK and we only get encrypted keys; you can revoke. For Dedicated and Private we can also support HSM-backed keys if required - that's the model most customers use when they need strict crypto control. There's a small setup for the key policy and IAM bindings.
[02:05] Speaker 2 (transcription): k v cash - sorry, KV cache - bucket for session state, is that persisted?
[02:11] Aisha: Good question. Markus?
[02:13] Markus: Our KV cache is ephemeral by default for hosted - we keep only what we need for inference; persistent caching can be enabled in dedicated deployments but it's configurable and encrypted. If you need no persistent state we can disable it.
[02:25] Lena: Audit logs - retention policy, and can we ship them to our SIEM in real time? Also need immutable logs for at least 2 years.
[02:32] Markus: Yes, logs are streamable. For hosted we can stream to your S3 bucket or push to a syslog endpoint; for dedicated/private there's an option for agent-based forwarding or direct VPC peering to your log collector. Immutability is customer-managed on your bucket (S3 Object Lock) but we provide signed delivery and digests to prove integrity. Retention windows are configurable; default is 90 days in the console but we can set longer retention for enterprise customers.
[02:55] Rajiv: On SSO, we use Okta with SCIM provisioning. How mature is your SCIM support? Can we sync groups for RBAC?
[03:03] Markus: We support SCIM 2.0 for user provisioning and group sync. You can map Okta groups to Redwood roles. We also have granular RBAC (role-based and resource-level policies) so you can map roles per team and per environment (prod/test).
[03:18] Tom: From procurement perspective, T&Cs: do you offer data processing addendums and contractual language around deletion and breach notification?
[03:25] Aisha: Yes, we include a DPA and standard breach notification SLA in our enterprise contract; we can surface those terms in the legal review.
[03:31] Lena: What about ISO 27001 - do you have that? Our vendor bar lists ISO as preferred.
[03:36] Markus: We're SOC 2 Type II today. ISO 27001 is on our roadmap and we're in the middle of the assessment process - I don't want to overclaim timelines, but we can share controls mapping between SOC 2 and ISO to help you evaluate coverage.
[03:49] Rajiv: For the dedicated option - is it single-tenant? How isolated is the network?
[03:54] Markus: Dedicated is a single-tenant GPU pool with isolated compute; you get VPC peering and no multi-tenant hypercall - network isolation is enforced and we provide private endpoints. For Private (VPC/on-prem) you get the control plane in your VPC and optionally an air-gapped on-prem runtime bundle.
[04:10] Lena: Our compliance folks will want to see architecture diagrams and a runbook for key compromise scenarios - e.g., what happens if an HSM key is suspected compromised.
[04:18] Markus: We'll provide a playbook: key rotation steps, revocation, and fallback to alternative models. For hosted BYOK, revoking the CMK will effectively block access to existing ciphertext until rekeyed, so we walk customers through revocation testing in staging.
[04:33] Aisha: Any red flags from your side, Summit?
[04:36] Lena: Main risk is the hosted model if we can't ensure EU-only data processing and KMS control. If Redwood can guarantee KMS in our account and logs in our S3 in EU, hosted could work. Otherwise we'll lean dedicated/private.
[04:50] Rajiv: Also want to run an initial perf/security POC to validate latencies and keys during heavy load.
[04:56] Markus: Totally doable. For POC we usually spin up a dedicated slice in your region, run reproducible load, and root-cause any policy frictions. We'll share a POC runbook.
[05:06] Tom: Pricing question - dedicated/pilot costs vs hosted - we need ballpark numbers before procurement sign-off.
[05:11] Aisha: We'll include a pricing worksheet with a dedicated pilot option and committed capacity numbers.
[05:16] Speaker 1 (transcription): There's also mention of Fed ramp from Lena but not required yet.
[05:22] Lena: Not now - maybe later.
[05:24] Aisha: Ok wrapping up. Quick recap of next steps: we'll send the SOC 2 Type II report and security questionnaire under NDA, Markus will produce architecture and KMS integration diagrams and a POC runbook, and we'll target a pilot call in the first week of January. Anything to add?
[05:38] Rajiv: Please include the data residency guarantees in writing.
[05:41] Lena: And a copy of your standard DPA.
[05:43] Tom: Procurement will need the TOC and pricing worksheet.
[05:46] Aisha: Great - we'll follow up. Thanks everyone!

End of transcript.

References / links mentioned: SOC 2 report (will be shared under NDA), security questionnaire (link to Redwood security pack), POC runbook (to be provided), architecture diagram (to be provided).
